newsitem.title: UK: UK forwarder warns airlines on cargo rate rises.
newsitem.headline: UK forwarder warns airlines on cargo rate rises.

text.p: Airlines have been warned by a major UK airfreight forwarder that they could lose increasing amounts of freight to shipping services if they persist in raising their cargo rates.

Gerry Burgin, managing director of Wilson & Co (UK), a unit of Sweden's Bilspedition Transport and Logistics, said a recent chronic shortage of cargo capacity on major long-haul routes had influenced airlines to announce fairly high rate increases.
"The air cargo industry has always been capacity driven, with the vast majority of freight flying on passenger aircraft," he told Reuters.

He said that over recent years, there have been more and more long- and middle-distance flights introduced which, because of their higher fuel loads, had offered considerably reduced cargo payload weight.

"Air cargo is a feast and famine business, dependent on the capacity available. The keyword now is 'famine' as there is a severe shortage of cargo capacity -- and has been for several months -- from the UK to Japan, Hong Kong, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and South America in particular," Burgin noted.

"Because of this situation, airlines have found themselves in the cargo industry driving seat. They are often operating at full capacity...they are being offered more cargo than they can carry", he said, persuading them to introduce often hefty rate rises.
However, he warned, the airlines should beware of implementing cargo rate increases too frequently and by too much.
"Naturally, we the forwarders are always concerned about the erosion of our already thin profit margins," he said.

But, Burgin stressed, there will come a point when shippers, who are both the airlines' and the forwarders' customers, will look at the rate situation closely and come to what might be an inevitable conclusion.
"They may before too long consider that the airlines are pricing themselves out of the market as far as certain commodities are concerned," he said.
"They will then seriously ask themselves just what cargo shipments can be moved from air to sea transportation," he said.
Airlines including Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Air France, British Airways Plc and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV have all recently announced spring cargo rate increases.
